title: Thermal entanglement transitions from strong $\textrm{SU}(2)$ symmetry
authors: Siqi Mo, Ehud Altman, Samuel J. Garratt
abstract: We study mixed-state entanglement in Gibbs states with strong $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ symmetry, focusing on locally interacting spin systems with ferromagnetic interactions. Our main result is to show that finite-temperature ordering transitions are associated with entanglement transitions, and therefore the steady state of strongly symmetric Lindbladians can exhibit entanglement transitions. While in the paramagnetic phase it is known that the distillable entanglement and logarithmic entanglement negativity between two halves of a large system grow logarithmically with the square root of the number of spins, we show that in ferromagnetic phases these quantities grow parametrically faster with system size. To arrive at this result we first establish relations between these mixed-state entanglement measures and spin correlations in states that are singlets under global $\rm{SU}(2)$ symmetry transformations. We then introduce a semiclassical theory for $\rm{SU}(2)$ singlet thermal states. While the global singlet constraint generally enters this theory as a complicated function of the full semiclassical spin configuration, we show that in large $S$ limit it simplifies drastically to a Gaussian suppression of total magnetization in disordered phases as well as in ordered phases in the vicinity of continuous thermal phase transitions. This leads us to a field theory describing spin correlations in the singlet sector. Using this we determine the behavior of various probes of mixed-state entanglement at low and at high temperatures, supporting our analytical results using numerical Monte Carlo simulations of a three-dimensional lattice realization of our semiclassical theory. We also use exact numerics in one-dimensional spin-$1/2$ systems to confirm our predictions for the scaling of mixed-state entanglement with correlation length and system size in the paramagnetic phase.
summary: This work analyzes mixed-state entanglement in spin systems possessing strong SU(2) symmetry, showing that thermal ordering transitions coincide with entanglement transitions. By developing a semiclassical theory, the authors prove that entanglement scaling changes dramatically between paramagnetic and ferromagnetic phases. This establishes a deep connection between the statistical mechanics of the system and its quantum information content.
main_problem: The study investigates how finite-temperature ordering transitions in strongly symmetric spin systems are directly linked to transitions in mixed-state entanglement.
main_result: The entanglement measures (distillable entanglement and logarithmic negativity) exhibit a transition in their system size scaling, moving from logarithmic to parametrically faster growth across the ferromagnetic phase transition.
method: The authors combine establishing relations between entanglement and spin correlations with developing a semiclassical theory for the singlet sector, which is verified using Monte Carlo and exact numerical simulations.
model_or_system: The system consists of locally interacting spin systems with ferromagnetic interactions, analyzed specifically within the total singlet sector ($	ext{SU}(2)$ symmetry). The analysis uses Gibbs states restricted to this singlet subspace.
key_observables: Mixed-state entanglement measures (distillable entanglement, logarithmic entanglement negativity) and spin correlations ($	ext{Tr}[ho_0 \vec{S}_i \cdot \vec{S}_j]$).
important_parameters: Temperature ($T$), system size ($N$), and the ferromagnetic coupling strength.
main_assumptions: The semiclassical theory is valid in the large $S$ limit, and the analysis relies on saddle-point approximations for path integrals.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the coincidence of thermal and entanglement transitions in the singlet sector, showing the scaling of the half-system spin ($\sim \sqrt{N}$ vs. $\sim N$) across the critical temperature $T_c$.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the connection between entanglement and correlations in the singlet sector, develops a semiclassical theory for the large $S$ limit, derives the scaling laws for entanglement measures, and finally confirms these predictions using numerical simulations and exact 1D calculations.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, quantitative link between macroscopic thermodynamic phase transitions (ordering) and quantum information measures (entanglement) in the context of open quantum systems dynamics.
